tour.pipelineBody: Someone stays a lead until they book and pay for a consultation. That is the only thing that converts them — not a status you set by hand, not a good phone call. It keeps the word "client" meaning one thing.
tour.bookingTitle: Your booking page does the intake
tour.bookingBody: Share one link. A client picks a time you actually have free, answers your questions, and uploads what you asked for. A contact, a project and a project code are created for you, and the slot can never be double-booked.
tour.stagesTitle: Ten stages, and gates that will not open early
tour.stagesBody: Every project walks the same ten stages. Some have gates — a contract stage will not close before the contract is signed and the deposit is in. You can override one, but you have to say why, and the reason is kept.
tour.documentsBody: Contracts, quotations, invoices and messages are generated from your templates with the client's details merged in, in Arabic or English, as PDF or Word. Nothing is ever sent for you — you copy or export it and send it yourself.
tour.portalBody: Your client sees their own progress, their published files, and can approve or ask for changes. They cannot see another project, another client, or anything else about your studio. Revoke the link and it dies instantly.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: The rules this product runs on, and why.
help.tourHint: The five-step introduction you saw when you first signed in.
help.stuckBody: Use the feedback button in the corner of any screen. It records which screen you were on, so we can see what you saw.
help.q_lead: Why will this lead not become a client?
help.a_lead: Because they have not booked a paid consultation yet. Booking is the only thing that converts a lead. If you moved them onto a booked status by hand, they will convert then — but the honest path is to let the booking do it.
help.q_booking: How does the booking page work?
help.a_booking: You set your available hours, session types and questions once. The link shows only slots you are genuinely free for, respects your notice period, and refuses a slot that was just taken by somebody else. Every booking creates a contact, a project and a project code.
help.q_code: Can I reuse a project code?
help.a_code: No. Codes are never reused, even if the project is deleted. A code on an old contract must always mean the same project.
help.a_stages: Every project walks the same path from consultation to follow-up. The order does not change between projects, which is what makes two projects comparable and lets the reports mean anything.
help.q_gate: Why will this stage not close?
help.a_gate: It has a gate that is not met yet — a contract not signed, a deposit not received, a client approval not given. The stage screen lists exactly what is missing. You can override it, but you must give a reason, and the reason is kept on the record.
help.a_documents: From your templates. The client's details are merged in and you get Arabic or English, PDF or Word. Edit the templates in Settings — editing one never changes a document you already generated.
help.q_sending: Does it email or WhatsApp my clients?
help.a_sending: Never. It writes the message and you send it yourself, from your own phone or inbox. The only emails this product sends are for your own account — confirming your address and resetting your password.
help.q_portal: What can my client see in the portal?
help.a_portal: Their own project: the stages, the progress, the files you published, the invoice, and a place to approve or request changes. Nothing else — not another project, not another client, not your contact list. Revoking the link cuts it off instantly, including downloads.
help.a_revisions: Each project has an allowance. When a client asks for a change through the portal it counts against it, and once the allowance is used up the portal tells them plainly that further changes are billable. It does not charge anything — there is no payment gateway anywhere in this product.
help.q_pricing: Which pricing method should I use?
help.a_pricing: Whichever suits the job. There are six and they are independent — per square metre, per room, percentage of cost, hourly, cost-plus and value-based. Use one, use none, ignore the rest. They do not affect each other.
help.q_deleting: I deleted a client by mistake.
help.a_deleting: Go to Settings, Recently deleted. Anything you delete waits there for 30 days and comes back exactly as it was, with the projects that went down with it.
